title: Enforce canonical core primitive boundary
summary: Require portable core and allocation primitives throughout rumiga-core, make the MAC-address error contract available without std, validate the rule under both explicit runtime profiles, and enforce the declared Rust MSRV for the stock no_std core graph.
scope: Desktop and no_std Clippy profile enforcement

risk.failure_mode: An over-broad portability rule could reject legitimate host adapters or a primitive substitution could alter desktop behavior.
risk.rollback: Revert the M1-003 core and CI commits together to restore the prior primitive imports and host matrix while retaining the existing runtime feature contract.

compatibility.detail: Default desktop behavior and runtime feature selection are unchanged; the shared MAC-address error contract is additionally available to no_std consumers.

security.detail: No network transport, credential, authorization, persistence, unsafe-code, or FFI behavior changes.

tests.proves: The desktop-selected core path rejects standard-library primitives with core or alloc equivalents.
The allocator-backed profile passes the core, integration, golden-vector, differential, and portable error-contract regressions.
The complete stock core graph remains an optimized bare-metal RISC-V no_std release build.
The complete stock core graph compiles with the workspace's declared Rust MSRV.
The canonical host gate runs strict Clippy for both core runtime profiles alongside the complete host baseline.

evidence.location: 2026-08-16 local execution: explicit std Clippy, no_std Clippy, 146 core unit tests plus applicable integration suites, the optimized stock-core bare-metal RISC-V release check, and the declared Rust 1.85 MSRV check passed.
evidence.proves: The implemented primitive boundary is locally valid before pull-request promotion.
